title: Pro-étale inverse image along a site object is slice restriction
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring, and $r\colon W\to X$ a morphism of schemes such that $W\xrightarrow{r}X$ is an object of the small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Identify $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the localization $X_{\mathrm{proét}}/W$ by the equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], and for a sheaf $G$ of sets, of abelian groups or of $A_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ write $G|_W$ for its restriction, $G|_W(U\to W)=G(U\to W\xrightarrow{r}X)$, with the restriction maps of $G$. Let $u_r$, the presheaf inverse image $u_{r,p}$, the inverse image $r^{-1}=(u_{r,p}-)^\#$, the structure map $c^r_A\colon r^{-1}A_X\to A_W$ and the module pullback $r^*G=r^{-1}G\otimes_{r^{-1}A_X}A_W$ be those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with $A_X,A_W$ the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then:

1. For every object $U\to W$ of $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the pair $(U\to W\xrightarrow{r}X,\ \varphi_0)$ with $\varphi_0=(\mathrm{str},\mathrm{id}_U)\colon U\to W\times_XU=u_r(U\to X)$ is an initial object of the indexing category $\mathcal I_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Consequently the coprojections indexed by these pairs give an isomorphism of presheaves $G|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{r,p}G$, natural in $G$, and the canonical map $u_{r,p}G\to r^{-1}G$ to the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is an isomorphism; thus $r^{-1}G\cong G|_W$ naturally in $G$, for sheaves of sets, of abelian groups and of rings.
2. Under this identification $r^{-1}A_X\cong A_X|_W$, the structure map $c^r_A$ is a ring isomorphism $A_X|_W\to A_W$, namely the inverse of the isomorphism $A_W\to A_X|_W$ of clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].
3. For every sheaf $G$ of $A_X$-modules there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $A_W$-modules $r^*G\cong G|_W$, natural in $G$, where $G|_W$ is an $A_W$-module through the isomorphism of (2); in particular the underlying abelian sheaf of $r^*G$ is that of $G|_W$.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products): for $U\in\mathcal C$ with products of pairs, $v(X)=X\times U/U$ defines the morphism of sites $\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ whose topos morphism is $j_U$ (inverse image = restriction); applied to the base-change functor of proetale.tex Tag 09A5. Pro-étale analogue of the DAG node lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction (étale case).

proof.text: Use composition left adjoint to base change. The distinguished structured arrow is its unit; the hom-set equivalence gives a unique arrow from it to every indexing object. This proves initiality directly.

Whisker the opposite site adjunction by the value category. Both precomposition by composition and the presheaf left Kan extension are left adjoints to precomposition by base change. Uniqueness of left adjoints yields the presheaf comparison. The homEquiv formula identifies its components with the distinguished coprojections, naturally in site objects and sheaves.

Restriction preserves sheaves. Transport the sheaf condition along the presheaf isomorphism; the sheafification unit of this already-sheaf presheaf is an isomorphism. Compose these maps and lift through the fully faithful sheaf inclusion to construct the specified normalized sheaf comparison.

Sheafification commutes with continuous cocontinuous composition restriction, giving the constant-ring localization isomorphism and its constant-section unit equation. To identify the specified coefficient map, use its inverse-image adjunction transpose, whose constant-presheaf normalization is definitional. Naturality at the distinguished index and the Kan-unit formula show that e followed by the inverse sheaf comparison and the coefficient map fixes constant sections. Sheafification uniqueness gives the identity, and cancellation gives the claimed coefficient equation.

The coefficient comparison equation proves the specified coefficient inverse-image map is an isomorphism. Sheafification uniqueness on constant presheaf sections proves that the normalized localization ring map and the specified direct-image coefficient map satisfy the unit and counit compatibility equations for composition left adjoint to base change. Forget commutativity and apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj, obtaining restriction left adjoint to the specified module direct image. The existing proEtaleRingModuleAdjunction is an adjunction for exactly the tensor-sheafification pullback in the statement. Its coefficient direct-image map equals the specified one by the ring adjunction inverse law. Uniqueness of left adjoints now gives the natural module isomorphism, with naturality inherited from that natural isomorphism. This proves the final clause and assembles the original conjunction.
